title: Trace anchoring for regression hunting
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a practical, tactical approach to "anchoring" traces to a compact set of high-signal metrics and dashboard widgets to accelerate regression hunting for tokenized inference (generation) regressions. Goal: reduce time-to-root-cause by giving oncall and SREs a small, repeatable set of traces + metric pivots to validate hypotheses.

Context / motivation:
- We have rich telemetry (latency histograms, kv-cache metrics, batch stats, model selection events, per-token logs) but too many signals. Investigations take too long because analysts run blind traces or surface-level dashboards that don't differentiate causes (model change, quantization mismatch, routing/fallback, client change).
- Anchoring = programmatic and UI-level linking of a small number of metric anchors to representative traces so that one click surfaces relevant traces pre-filtered by the anchor context.

What an anchor is (working definition):
- A metric and a short filter expression that, when elevated above a threshold, defines a cohort of requests to fetch traces for.
- Example: "latency_p99 > 600ms AND model_variant:quantized-ggml-v2 AND kv_cache_hit=false" -> anchor cohort.

Recommended metric anchors (prioritized):
1) Path-level p99 generation latency (ms) - label by model, region, route. Use delta vs. baseline to detect regressions.
2) Model fallback count - counts of requests that hit fallback routing (e.g., to smaller model or different quantization) in last 5m.
3) KV-cache cold rate - fraction of requests with KV cache miss on first token.
4) Batch-size effective distribution - median and p95 of batch size for a route (detects batching collapse).
5) Per-token decode time p95 - isolates slow decoding (kernel/hardware).
6) Tokenization error ratio - rate of tokenization failures or fallback tokenizers.
7) Client-side prompt-length spikes - 95th percentile of prompt token count per route.

Metric definitions (compact canonical strings for instrumentation and dashboards):
- gen.latency.p99{route,model_variant,region} = 99th percentile of end-to-end generate() duration measured at gateway (ms)
- routing.fallback.count{route,model_variant} = count of requests routed to fallback target in window
- kvcache.miss_rate{route,tenant} = sum(kv_miss_count)/sum(kv_access_count) over 5m window
- batching.effective_median{route} = median(batch_size_effective) over 5m
- decode.time.p95{device_type,model_variant} = 95th percentile of per-token decode step time on serving device (ms/token)
- tokenizer.error_ratio{route} = count(tokenizer_errors)/count(requests)

Trace anchoring patterns (how to attach traces to anchors):
- Anchor -> Sampling override: when an anchor threshold trips, increase sampling rate for traces matching the anchor filters for 10 minutes. Record anchor id in trace metadata.
- Anchor -> Direct trace query: UI should pre-compose a trace query that applies the anchor filters and time window and returns top N traces sorted by error or duration.
- Anchor -> Breadcrumb enrichment: Insert a lightweight breadcrumb span at request edge containing anchor labels (route, model_variant, batch_id, kv_cache_hit) to make trace joins cheap.

Examples of anchor filter expressions (UI-friendly syntax):
- gen.latency.p99{route:chat-complete,model_variant:open-8b} > 500
- kvcache.miss_rate{tenant:acme} > 0.35 AND batching.effective_median{route:embed} < 2
- decode.time.p95{device_type:gpu-a100} > 1.2 AND routing.fallback.count{route:chat-stream} > 5

Dashboard widgets to support anchors (minimal, top-of-oncall page):
- Anchor health table: row per anchor with current value, 1h delta, threshold, and one-click "open traces" button.
- Funnel widget: new requests -> cache hit -> batched -> model selected -> served. Show dropoff rates and absolute counts.
- Cohort latency heatmap: rows = models, columns = routes, cells = gen.latency.p95 with sparkline trend.
- Representative trace list: for selected anchor, show 10 traces with key tags (batch size, kv cache, model_variant, request size).
- Diff panel: compare selected time window vs baseline for top 3 anchors (p95/p99, fallback rate, cache miss).

Investigation playbook (short walkthrough):
1) Detection: Pager fires on gen.latency.p99 (route=chat-complete) > 2x baseline -> oncall lands on anchor health table.
2) Anchor triage: click anchor -> UI returns representative traces, sorted by duration and error.
3) Quick checks (5 min):
   - Are traces showing long decode spans or long queue spans? If decode spans dominated -> suspect serving runtime/kernel issues.
   - Is KV cache miss rate elevated for these traces? If yes, check upstream cache invalidation/deployment.
   - Are model variant labels inconsistent with expected rollout? If many traces show an unexpected variant, check rollout/flags.
4) Hypothesis test (10 min): use trace filters to isolate single variable, e.g., filter to device_type=gpu-a100 and model_variant=quantized-ggml-v2 to see if latency normalizes.
5) Remediation steps: rollback model rollout, increase routing capacity for particular variant, enable temporary cache warm paths, or revert kernel change.
6) Postmortem signals to capture: exact anchor expression that tripped, top 5 trace ids, diff screenshots from dashboard, snapshot of rollout state (git tag, deploy id).

Instrumentation guidance (practical):
- Add an anchor breadcrumb span within the gateway at request acceptance: include route, tenant, model_variant, prompt_token_count, batch_id, kv_cache_hit boolean. Keep payload <= 128 bytes.
- Emit gen.latency.* at gateway (includes queue+decode+network to client); also emit device-level decode.time.* inside runtime with same request_id so traces can correlate.
- Ensure model variant is a stable tag (avoid using long commit sha in tag; use human-friendly variant names with optional build metadata separate).

Retention and sampling policy recommendations:
- Default trace sampling: 0.5% global for production routes.
- Anchor triggered sampling: 100% for matching requests for 10 minutes, then back to 5% for next 30 minutes (to capture replays).
- Retain full traces for 30 days for anchor-triggered records; keep compact span summaries for 90 days.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How to express multi-anchor correlation (e.g., anchor A and anchor B tripped together) in a compact UI? (product mock needed)
- Should we auto-create alerts for anchors that have repeated trips within a week? (ops governance)
- Decide retention/ingest cost guardrails for anchors to avoid trace bill shock.

Next concrete steps (action items):
- Engineering: prototype anchor breadcrumb span + sampling override (owner: Priya, ETA: 2025-10-01).
- Product/Obs: mock a minimal "Anchor health table" UI in Grafana or internal console (owner: Liam, ETA: 2025-09-24).
- SRE: pick initial set of 6 anchors (from list above) and codify thresholds by route (owner: Zoe, ETA: 2025-09-18).
